avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, and the fight against emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: This year, the City is paying companies to plant and maintain trees on streets and in parks, and it is funding an organization that plants on private and institutional land. Boroughs are adding their own money, machinery and teams of employees to plant trees. Two boroughs have also allowed construction projects to depart from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.titre: Contracts to plant trees on streets
etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees on public land, then to water, maintain and replace some of them. The authorized spending is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, and the trees go into seven boroughs, including Saint-Laurent (423), Verdun (281) and Pierrefonds-Roxboro (265).

etapes.titre: Money to plant on private property
etapes.texte: The City is paying $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026. The organization and its Alliance forêt urbaine partners must plant 14,500 trees and 2,500 shrubs in 2026.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its parks fund to buy trees and plants. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe with operator for $152,916.75 and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams, aiming to plant about 1,000 trees in 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve allows a company to expand its building at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening, instead of the required 40 trees and 25%, with the company offsetting this on its other properties. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

etapes.titre: Work at parc Pratt, in Outremont
etapes.texte: Outremont awards URBEX CONSTRUCTION INC. the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, water retention and new pathways. The authorized spending is $800,416.17, taxes included, funded mainly by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit progress reports on July 31 and October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve's tree plantings take place from April or May to November 2026.
Watering, maintenance and replacement of trees planted under the central city's contract continue until the end of November 2029.

deneigement.description: Contracts for snow removal and snow loading, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Several boroughs rented suction sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operator to remove abrasives in the spring. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorized $574,920.99, taxes included, for four sweepers and three tanker trucks in 2026 and 2027 [CA26 27 0008].

etapes.titre: Snow removal from downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie awarded companies the maintenance, cleaning and snow removal of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises and six other public squares, including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough also extended snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, until April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

etapes.titre: Additional funding and staff for the 2025-2026 season
etapes.texte: Montréal-Nord paid $106,150.97 more for the rental of an additional grader during the winter of 2025-2026 [CA26 10 086], and Saint-Léonard drew $200,000 from its surpluses for staff and the purchase of salt and sand [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun offered city council to provide the staff for its snow disposal site itself.

etapes.titre: Extensions decided by the central city
etapes.texte: City council and the executive committee extended by 12 months the turnkey snow removal contracts of Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, the towing contracts of four boroughs, the equipment rental in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie and the snow removal of a parking lot in Montréal-Est. The extension of the turnkey contracts costs $7,399,240.83, taxes included [CM26 0548].

Ville-Marie extended the rental of tractor-loaders with operators for the winter of 2026-2027 and allocated $323,361.50 from its surpluses [CA26 240129]. Ahuntsic-Cartierville renewed the rental of a compact loader tractor and Anjou renewed the rental of a grader.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Léonard indicates that the adoption of its snow removal by-law is scheduled for September 8, 2026, with a notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.
The extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.
The rental of equipment with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie starts on November 1, 2026 and runs until March 31, 2027.
The rental of a grader in Anjou covers November 15, 2026 to April 15, 2027.
Snow removal for the parking lot of the édifice Jacinthe-Fyfe is extended from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is borrowing to finance the disinfection plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant and new main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane sector. It is awarding contracts to rehabilitate water pipes without trenching, rebuild streets along with their sewers and waterworks, and replace lead water service connections. It is also adding amounts to projects already underway and purchasing the products and services needed to run its plants.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining, a trenchless technique, and to redo roadways and sidewalks on streets in several boroughs. These contracts also include the replacement of lead water service connections, on both the public and private sides.

The City is adding money to contracts already awarded: $200,000 in contingencies for boulevard De Maisonneuve (CA26 240015) and $1,055,231.53 for the 750 mm pipe on rue Saint-Antoine Ouest (CG26 0153). It is also adding $12,144,522.14 in contingencies for the pipe on rue de la Cathédrale, after an inspection revealed more damaged sections than in 2019 (CG26 0336).

Contracts are awarded to redo water pipes, sewers and roadways together, notably along rue Guy between Saint-Jacques and René-Lévesque, for a total expenditure of $28,921,033.25 (CG26 0245), and on rue De Champlain, where a 1,200 mm main pipe installed in 1927 is being replaced (CG26 0332). Other similar projects affect Saint-Laurent, Lachine, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Pierrefonds-Roxboro.

etapes.titre: Plants, wastewater treatment plant and new loan
etapes.texte: The City is renewing support for the system that controls the processes at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant, extending the purchase of polymers for this plant, adding aluminum sulphate for the Pointe-Claire drinking water production plant, and extending leak detection by probe in main pipes. It is also adopting a $12,000,000 loan to build main waterworks pipes between boulevard Cavendish and rue Isabella, in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

aSurveiller.texte: The pipe along autoroute 15 Nord and the Atwater ramp must be rehabilitated by no later than December 18, 2026.
Work on rue de la Cathédrale, up to the McTavish reservoir, must be completed by March 2027.
The rue Guy project must continue until December 2027.
Leak detection in main pipes must be completed by June 2028.
Commissioning of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant is expected in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, and electrical upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel: a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, the modernization of electrical installations linked to biogas capture, and park maintenance. It is also asking Québec for financial help for an east-west pedestrian and bike link with a footbridge. At the same time, the borough is redoing rue De Louvain, along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Request for funding for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for help of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge about 150 metres long (CG26 0121). The project also includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The urban agglomeration approves construction of a research, training and community production greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then delegates the project to city council (CG26 0124). The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry it out and city council accepts (CA26 14 0039, CM26 0363).

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract of $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, which includes new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture (CG26 0223). It also hires two companies for general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months (CG26 0224).

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work involves sewers and water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, for $296,349.21 more, taxes included. The compost, made from leaves collected in parks and streets, is used in particular for the development of parc Frédéric-Back (CG26 0320).

The borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. the supply and installation of the greenhouse complex, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $574,845.80. The project covers two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, soils, interior divisions and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouses: delivery of infrastructure in July 2026, work starting in August 2026 and expected completion in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
Greenhouses commissioning announced for winter 2027.
The call for projects under the ministère des Transports' assistance program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Rue De Louvain: work in three phases, from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Park maintenance: contracts from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Rental of the screener and loader tractor from June 20 to October 15, 2026.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the stone walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. to rebuild heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, surplus mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work, 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, resumes on May 15, 2026.

etapes.titre: Application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques night sky
etapes.texte: The City is filing the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. Filing the application involves no expense; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan, upgrading its light fixtures to standard, and keeping the site accessible in the evening.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération, along with conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 report on areas.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. the contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche, for a total expense of $481,850.45. The work includes the new culvert, roadway repairs and replacement of the safety guardrails.

aSurveiller.texte: Expected end of work on the chemin de Senneville stone walls: July 10, 2026.
Filing of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan: February 2027.
Response from DarkSky International on the designation: April 2027.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warm-up spaces and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings for free to organizations so they can open warm-up spaces, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. A Ville-Marie public works team carries out cleanliness interventions related to homelessness in other boroughs, which accept the offer one by one. The City is also adopting a framework to receive private cash donations intended for shelter and housing.

etapes.titre: Two buildings lent for the winter
etapes.texte: The City lends the former Sainte-Bibiane church, at 5600, 12e Avenue, free of charge to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal for a warm-up space for women, from December 15, 2025 to April 30, 2026. It is also lending the former Recluses Missionnaires monastery, at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est, to Projets Autochtones du Québec until April 30, 2026, and is transferring $97,000 from the Service de l'habitation to the Service de la gestion et de la planification des immeubles for building costs (CG26 0066).

The City lends the former Bain St-Denis, at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert, free of charge to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN for a warm-up space open from 4 p.m. to 8 a.m., seven days a week, for 90 days starting February 1, 2026. The value of the loan is estimated at $56,978 (CG26 0116).

etapes.titre: Contracts and workers in the boroughs
etapes.texte: Verdun is paying $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two psychosocial workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is increasing to $126,615.07, taxes included, the contract awarded to Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. to run a warm-up space during the winter of 2025-2026.

The City is granting $5,407,736 to 15 organizations and an additional $3,942,461 to 10 already-funded organizations, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for projects ending December 31, 2028. The projects focus on the inclusion of people experiencing homelessness, cohabitation in public spaces and awareness-raising.

City council is adopting a framework to receive private financial contributions intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation: donors do not choose which project gets funded, and the City may refuse a donation. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is transferring $250,000 from its surplus for improvement work on the temporary warm-up space at Bain Saint-Denis. City council is adopting a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion from the Opposition officielle on a municipal rent support fund.

aSurveiller.texte: The agreement on the public works team accepted by Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
The financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and social, affordable or student housing projects, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: The City approves the 2026 budgets of the SHDM and the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, transfers or purchases land for social housing and pays grants to organizations that build affordable housing. It also amends the by-law that requires developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.texte: City council approves the 2026 budget of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal, which manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units. The urban agglomeration council approves that of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, which houses 42,587 households.

The City obtains from the Government of Canada, at no cost, half the rights over a 3,658.8 square-metre site on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro. It also transfers, at no cost, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a site at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, where 26 housing units are to be built.

The City signs two funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec for temporary housing and housing search assistance. It adds $877,312 to its assistance to Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors and grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project.

After a public consultation meeting held on February 26, 2026, city council amends the by-law on social, affordable and family housing: it will now only apply to projects larger than 18,000 square metres and will require 20% non-market housing units. Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its by-law on fees for temporary occupation of public property related to social and affordable housing projects.

etapes.titre: Purchase of a site in Le Sud-Ouest
etapes.texte: The City buys, for $9,293,113, a vacant 1,535.1 square-metre site east of rue Chatham and north of rue William, for social housing purposes. It also removes eleven lots in Ville-Marie and Le Sud-Ouest from the list of properties subject to the right of first refusal for social housing.

etapes.titre: 350 housing units in Angus, 72 housing units in Rosemont
etapes.texte: The City grants $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel to build 350 affordable housing units at the Technopôle Angus. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build a 72-unit building on the "Solotech" site, on 2e Avenue.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline for the sale of the site at rues Chatham and William: August 12, 2026.
SHDM project on 2e Avenue: public call for tenders in late summer or early fall 2026, construction start by the end of 2026, delivery in May 2028.
Affordable housing units at Technopôle Angus: occupancy expected by April 30, 2027 at the latest.
Construction sites announced by the SHDM: De Maisonneuve in Ville-Marie in spring 2026, Jardin des Prairies in fall 2026, and a 72-unit project at the corner of Gilford and 2e Avenue in fall 2026.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: City council amended two leases for land south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent: a 2,787-square-metre lot leased to the Société de transport de Montréal for $49,293 total, and an 836-square-metre lot leased to a paid-parking company for $45,049 before taxes.

The City is extending, free of charge, the loan of a 10,000-square-foot lot to an organization that grows a vegetable garden there, and a 3,316-square-metre lot to an urban agriculture organization for sunflowers and a greenhouse. City council also agreed to prepare itself a free lease for 78,244 square feet, at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade, for event activities.

etapes.titre: Contract to redevelop rue de Louvain
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes, and authorized a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. The work involves sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name came from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Events and programming on the site
etapes.texte: The borough granted $35,000 to an organization to design and carry out the Esplanade-Louvain pop-up space, at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, from June 9 to December 31, 2026. It also authorized, on a vacant lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, an event-based and temporary use: multimedia activity, shows, street food, alcohol service and recreational activities.

etapes.titre: New street, networks and rehabilitated soil
etapes.texte: The City awarded a company a $10,311,940.25 contract, including taxes, to build a street with sewer, water main, roadway, lighting and soil management in the eco-district, for a total expenditure of $15,366,336, and added $2,007,312.15 net to rehabilitate the soil of the former gas station area. The borough also adopted a second draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest and the construction of a group of buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: The rue de Louvain worksite between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel will proceed in three phases: from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, and then from May to August 2028.
The loan of the land for the sunflowers and greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2027.
The lease for the event activities covers two periods from April 1 to October 31, in 2026 and 2027.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named by the end of the development, expected around 2032.
The parking lease with the Société de transport de Montréal begins October 1, 2026, for three years, with a maximum of 92 days per year.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanation and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: The City has changed collection schedules and frequencies in several boroughs, and extended contracts for food waste treatment, container collection and container transport for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre. It also purchased collection bins, awarded companies hydro-excavation work with waste material treatment, and received the 2025 waste material management reports.

etapes.texte: The City extended by six months two contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to treat food waste, with an additional expense of $3,269,055.43 including taxes [CG26 0045]. It also extended by 12 months the contracts for garbage collection in front-loading and semi-underground containers, and the contract for the supply and transport of containers for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre.

The executive committee changed the collection days, schedules and sectors in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and every week from May 1 to October 31 [CE26 0466].

The City entered into agreements with USD Global inc., Orbis Canada ltée and Plasti-Bac inc. to supply and distribute collection bins for residents. Ahuntsic-Cartierville hired Ville en vert to inform and raise awareness among residents of buildings with eight units or fewer in the Ahuntsic and Sault-au-Récollet districts, where the garbage collection frequency is changing, for $230,108.67 including taxes [CA26 09 0141].

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal authorized the removal of two dwelling units in the basement of 397 boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest to set up a waste material storage room of at least 28 m² and 32 bicycle spaces. Le Sud-Ouest lifted the requirement to set up a drop-off area on the site of the future building at 2380 rue Notre-Dame Ouest, and the executive committee approved an agreement with Tricentris, which is paying $43,773.61 for a program to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations.

The urban agglomeration council took note of the 2025 waste material management report and the accountability report of the 2020-2025 Master Plan: 415 kg of waste per person, 48% of materials diverted from disposal, and 29 of 49 actions completed [CG26 0311]. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Saint-Laurent and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce filed their expense reports for the activities delegated to them.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until September 30, 2026.
The container collection contracts and the Saint-Laurent ecocentre container contract are maintained until October 31, 2027.
The reusable dishware, water fountain and sorting station loan program is offered until December 31, 2026, at the latest.
The hydro-excavation contracts end on December 31, 2028.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water main in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government is granting the City a deadline until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not entail any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer remain the same.

The City is guaranteeing a $2,000,000 loan from the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, a non-profit organization, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. That same day, city council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and management of the neighbourhood's public assets.

City council adopts a $29,000,000 loan by-law for soil remediation, sewers and water mains, street redevelopment, professional fees and land purchases. This work must serve the first lots of phase 1, intended for social, community and affordable housing.

A second loan by-law, for $12,000,000, finances the construction of main water lines between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It covers plans and specifications, soil studies, surveying, decontamination, land purchases and a first batch of work.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: deadline set by the Québec government to sell a first piece of land on the site.
2031: the $128.3M federal subsidy is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by this date.

parcs.description: Development and rehabilitation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is having parks redone in a number of places across its territory: play areas, water games, trails, sports fields and dog parks. It is awarding design and construction contracts, adjusting contracts already underway, and paying for the decontamination of land where parks will be built. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is repairing structures, submitting an application for an international designation, and listing a sector in the directory of protected natural environments.

etapes.texte: The City is entrusting the winning team of an architecture competition with the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil studies before redoing the play areas of parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former dump.

etapes.titre: Works and protection in the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for the rehabilitation of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and is awarding a contract to rebuild a culvert under that same road, in the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and is listing the Anse-à-l'Orme sector in the directory of protected natural environments.

The boroughs are awarding contracts to redo parks: parc à chien Lucie-Bruneau in Anjou, parc Mackenzie-King in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, parc canin Alexis-Nihon in Saint-Laurent, parc Monseigneur-Langlois in Verdun, and parc Percy-Walters in Ville-Marie. Outremont is paying $150,000 to redo the play structure at the parc-école Saint-Germain.

City council is transferring a section of the former rue Eadie, measuring 810.2 m², to parc Campbell Ouest, in the Sud-Ouest. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a construction contract for parc Denise-Morelle and paying a supplement to the project's architects, while LaSalle is entrusting the redevelopment of parc J.O.R.-Leduc.

aSurveiller.texte: Parc des Eaux-Cachées public art competition: winner chosen in October 2026, contract in December 2026, installation of the artwork in 2028.
Urban Night Sky Place application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance work in April 2032.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: final acceptance of the work expected in June 2027.
Parc Denise-Morelle: work from early August 2026 to November 2026.
Parc J.O.R.-Leduc: work from August 2026 to June 2028.
Parc Percy-Walters: work from July to November 2026, with a continuation in spring 2027.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and business animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are organizing the pedestrian streets for summer 2026: funding for boroughs and business development corporations, then ordinances that close streets to cars and set rules for terraces, sales, music and signage. Temporary public squares are also being set up, and support services are being added, such as on-demand transit on avenue du Mont-Royal.

etapes.titre: Grant framework and end of a lawsuit
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its business development corporations for pedestrianizing streets in 2026, up to $425 per linear metre. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to public square work at the corner of rues Beaubien Est and Boyer.

The executive committee pays $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries. Ville-Marie and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopt their first ordinances, including the Placette CDN, open from April 1 to October 31, 2026.

Ville-Marie grants $375,500 to the Société de développement commercial du Village for rue Sainte-Catherine Est, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension $102,045 for rue Villeray. Outremont sets aside $105,000 for avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique.

Outremont closes avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24, 2026. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce turns avenues Royal and Madison into pedestrian streets and public squares from June 1 to October 31, 2026. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal bans amplified instruments and playing between 9 p.m. and 8 a.m. on pedestrianized avenues. The City pays $40,000 to animate the rue Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street from July 10 to 19, 2026, and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a business promotion on avenue de Monkland.

aSurveiller.texte: Animation of the rue Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street from July 10 to 19, 2026; the organization must submit its accountability report by August 31, 2026, at the latest.
Avenue de Monkland closed to traffic from August 19 at 10 p.m. to August 24 at 7 a.m., with activities from August 20 to 23, 2026.
Avenue Lacombe closed to cars from September 10 to 13, 2026.
Rue Ontario Est pedestrianized until September 18, 2026; parking meters return on September 17, 2026.
Avenue Bernard fully reopened to traffic as of September 25, 2026.
Placette CDN and avenues Royal and Madison: traffic returns after October 31, 2026, namely November 1, 2026, for the placette.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, following public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of buildings of heritage interest, regulates housing and service establishments for people experiencing residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration plans. A public meeting was held on March 18, 2026 and a written consultation ran from March 11 to March 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and building coverage ratio in the area bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the plans for view corridors and heights; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and requires approval for certain work within the declared heritage site of the Mont-Royal.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, following a public consultation meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève states it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other batches have been announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood stations, city council motions.
securite-publique.enBref: This year, the City is funding equipment for the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) through a loan by-law and is awarding purchase and service contracts: motorcycles, practice ammunition, meals for detained persons, building and software maintenance. It is also renewing leases for neighbourhood stations, the training centre and parking spaces, and is lending police officers to the Gendarmerie royale du Canada and the Sûreté du Québec. Several borough councils have adopted motions of support for the SPVM following the shooting of June 22, 2026.

etapes.titre: Vehicles, building and services for the SPVM
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council is purchasing 11 motorcycles for road patrol, replacing the oil heating at the cavalry station at 1515, chemin Remembrance, and awarding the meals for detained persons to a new supplier. It is also extending the janitorial services at headquarters and the maintenance of the call dispatch system software.

The executive committee is authorizing the SPVM to receive a $8,000 grant from the Department of Justice of Canada. The money funds video segments in the métro and a police kiosk during the Victims and Survivors of Crime Week, from May 11 to 15, 2026.

etapes.titre: Leases for stations and the training centre
etapes.texte: The City is renewing the leases for neighbourhood station 15, rue de l'Église in Verdun, and neighbourhood station 26, avenue Mountain Sights in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It is also extending the lease of the SPVM training centre, rue Ernest-Cormier in Anjou, and leasing 50 parking spaces at 260, boulevard De Maisonneuve for headquarters vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: "Beans and Pork" fundraising day at neighbourhood station 46, on October 23, 2026.
Completion of the heating replacement work at the cavalry station, on September 30, 2027.
The City plans to replace the SPVM's call dispatch system at the end of 2027.
New lease term for the training centre, rue Ernest-Cormier, starting November 1, 2033.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, station surroundings, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approved the budget and capital works program of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), then a loan by-law from the company. It also sold or leased land to the STM to expand metro facilities, entrusted the STM with work related to the extension of the blue line, and set the framework for construction sites in the metro tunnel. It also signed a letter of non-objection for the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopted the STM's 2026 budget, balanced at $1,804,314,410 in both revenues and expenses, and the 2026-2035 capital works program. City council gave the same direction.

The City entered into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie for clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, following a call for tenders by the STM. It also purchased, without a call for tenders, advertising space from Astral Affichage in the metro and on buses for Espace pour la vie, up to $172,462.50 including taxes.

The City is leasing to the STM a 2,787-square-metre lot in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, south of rue de Louvain, as parking for vehicles of officers with a permit, for a total rent of $49,293. The same borough modified bus waiting posts on its territory as part of the network overhaul.

The City signed an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion in Parc Irma-LeVasseur, backing onto the metro ventilation station on avenue Wiseman, in Outremont. It also entrusted the STM with carrying out its municipal work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, for an expenditure of $3,808,451.29 including taxes.

Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce signed a new access agreement with the STM for a vacant lot of 3,274.2 square metres at 4636-4670, boulevard Décarie, and terminated the 2024 transitional occupancy agreement. Ville-Marie authorized the STM to drill and restore the vault of the green line tunnel, between Berri-UQAM and Saint-Laurent, 24 hours a day.

aSurveiller.texte: Drilling and restoration work on the vault of the green line tunnel until July 31, 2026.
Awarding of contracts for the Pie-IX and Viau stations in August and October 2026; opening of the blue line extension stations planned for 2031.
Start of the STM parking lease on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
Work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, until December 2027.
Complete closure of rue Wilderton, for a maximum of two weeks, during the summer holidays of 2027; reconstruction work on the bridge-tunnel from June 2026 to March 2028.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and lanes, and the bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bikes, docks and station parts for the BIXI system, and is having new stations installed as part of street construction projects. It is also funding the rehabilitation of existing bike paths, including the REV Lajeunesse, and is regularizing rents for Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. For their part, boroughs oversee the development and maintenance of their bike paths.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes a $100,000 expenditure, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives intended in particular for bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the rental of a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide, for $153,395.05, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Sustainable mobility corridors in the east
etapes.texte: City council adds $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for traffic lights, civil and electrical work and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on rue Hochelaga and rue du Havre. The contract reaches $11,399,999.99, taxes included.

City council approves a $125,167.62 agreement, taxes included, with Hydro-Québec for rents from 2014 to 2025 on 19 pieces of land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, with total rent of $46,896, taxes included, to rent approximately 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for a bike path.

etapes.titre: Rehabilitation of the REV Lajeunesse and rue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of the rehabilitation of sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for roadway and bike path work under the Plan Vélo 2019. Outremont tables a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: For the REV Lajeunesse, the file indicates a call for tenders in May 2026, contract awards in June, and work from July to August 2026.
The UCI Road World Championships are held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; sections along the route are targeted by roadway work in Ville-Marie.
The rehabilitation of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is listed at $570,000 in 2027.
Work on the sustainable mobility corridors resumes in spring 2026, for delivery in spring or summer 2026.
